Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 1:

Tafsir of Surat al-Muddaththir

It is Meccan.

Jabir ibn Abd Allah mentioned that it was the first surah to be revealed of the Qur'an.

It is also narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I secluded myself in Hira' for a month. When I had completed it and came down into the valley, I was called, 'O Muhammad!' I looked in front of me, behind me, to my right and to my left, and I saw no one. I was called again, and again, and again. I raised my head, and behold, it was in the Throne, in the air." 

That is, Jibril (peace be upon him). "So I trembled with terror, returned to the house, and said: 'Wrap me up, cover me!'"

In another narration: "Pour cold water over me." Then Jibril came to me and said: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn﴾.

It is well known that the first thing revealed of the Qur'an was the surah Iqra' (Read), and we will explain what follows. It is possible to reconcile the two narrations by saying: Surat Iqra' was the first of the Qur'an to be revealed when revelation began, and Surat al-Muddaththir was the first to be revealed after the pause in revelation (fatrat al-wahy). And Allah knows best.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ means: O you who wrap yourself (al-mutadaththir), like His saying: ﴿O you who are wrapped in garments﴾ (al-muzzammil), meaning al-mutazammil.

The difference between al-shi'ar (the undergarment) and al-dithar (the outer garment) is that al-shi'ar is the garment that is next to a person's skin, and al-dithar is the garment that is over that.

Ma'mar narrated from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speak about the pause in revelation, and he said in his narration: "While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my head, and behold, the angel who had come to me at Hira' was sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I trembled with terror from him, returned, and said: 'Wrap me up, cover me!' Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾." This report is agreed upon as authentic.

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: We were informed of it by Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad; we were informed by Abu Sahl Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar; we were informed by Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya [al-Adhrafi]; we were informed by Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari; we were informed by Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar... the report.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 2:

The Most High's words: ﴿Arise and warn﴾. Abu al-Husayn Ibn Faris said: "Qiyam (standing up) in the language of the Arabs has two senses: qiyam of jadd (earnest resolve) and qiyam of intisab (standing upright). The qiyam of intisab is well known, and the qiyam of jadd and 'azm (resolve) is like the saying of the poet:

(We have accepted him, so arise and be firm...)

He said it concerning one of the caliphs regarding some of the heirs to the caliphate (wulat al-'ahd)."

Al-Dahhak said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was reclining, so he rose." ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, that is, the sleeper.

﴿Arise and warn﴾, that is: arise from sleep and warn the people.

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord, glorify Him with greatness﴾ means: magnify Him. The fa' (فَ) has entered here with the sense of the response to a conditional.

It was also said: "Your Lord, so say: Allah is greater (Allahu akbar)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿And your garments, purify﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah said its meaning is: do not wear them while treacherous and sinful.

Al-Suddi said: "And your deeds, correct them."

The poet said regarding the first view:

(And by the praise of God, I have never worn a sinful garment, nor have I covered myself with a treachery.)

Al-Suddi said: The Arabs say, "So-and-so has clean garments" when his deeds are good, and "So-and-so has soiled garments" when his deeds are wicked.

It was also said: "And your garments, purify" means: "your heart, correct it."

Imru' al-Qays said:

(If you have been displeased with me for some conduct, then ask my garments about your garments, and they will slip away from you.)

Tawus said: "And your garments, purify" means: shorten them, for when a garment is long it drags on the ground, and so it is struck by what makes it impure.

Umar, concerning a man who dragged his garment, said: "Shorten your garments, for that is cleaner, more lasting, and more pious."

From Ibn Sirin, regarding His saying ﴿And your garments, purify﴾, it means: [wash them] from impurities.

This is the view preferred by the jurists.

Al-Zajjaj mentioned that purification here is shortening, as we mentioned from Tawus.

It was also said: "And your women, correct them," meaning: marry chaste believing women.

We have already explained that clothing is used as a metaphor for women, so it is likewise permissible for garments to be understood in this way.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 74, verse 5:**

And His saying: ﴿And uncleanness, shun﴾. Mujahid and Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i) said its meaning is: "shun" (fa-hjur), i.e., keep away. The second opinion: concerning the idols, "shun" them, and this is a well-known view.

It has also been recited as "wa-l-rujz fa-hjur" (with the letter ra' and the zay) for this meaning.

Al-Farra' said: al-rujz and al-rijz (with a kasra or damma on the ra') have the same meaning.

It has been said: al-rujz is al-rijs (filth), meaning: avoid filth and impurities.

And according to this opinion, the sin (in al-rujz) was replaced by a zay.

It is also said: al-rujz is the punishment (al-adhab), and the meaning is: avoid what leads to punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 6:

And His saying ﴿And do not bestow favor, seeking to receive more﴾. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And do not bestow favor that you may receive more."

Al-Kisa'i said: the word "an" (that) has been dropped, so the verb is in the nominative (marfu').

Al-Hasan said its meaning is: do not bestow favor upon anyone with your giving.

The mention of seeking to receive more is because one only bestows favor when he sees it as much.

The well-known view is: do not give to anyone in order to receive more than what you give.

Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i) said: this applies specifically to the Prophet (ﷺ), because Allah the Exalted commanded him with the noblest manners and the most exalted character; as for others, there is no harm in it.

Al-Mughirah ibn Muqsim al-Dabbi related it from Ibrahim.

And this which we have mentioned has been reported from other than Ibrahim.

And His saying: ﴿And for your Lord, be patient﴾. Mujahid said: "Patient over what you are harmed by."

It was also said: "Patient in upholding the truth and conveying the message."

And it is related from Ibrahim, who said: "And for your Lord, be patient," until you are rewarded for your deed.

Al-Nahhas cited it from him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 8:

Allah the Exalted's saying ﴿So when the Trumpet is sounded﴾ means: the Ṣūr (the Trumpet).

It is also said: it is the first blowing (al-nafkha al-ūlā).

It is also said: it is the second blowing (al-thāniya).

It has been narrated that Zurārah ibn Abī Awfā used to lead a people in prayer, and he recited ﴿So when the Trumpet is sounded﴾ and fell down unconscious (mughshiyan ʿalayhi).

It is also said: it [al-nāqūr] resembles the horn (al-būq).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 9:

And His saying: ﴿So that Day, that will be a difficult day﴾, i.e., severe.
﴿Upon the disbelievers, it will be no easy matter.﴾ That is: not easy, nor lenient.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 11:

﴿The Exalted said: "Leave me with the one whom I created alone (wahidan)." His saying "Leave me" (dharni) means: leave me (da'ni).

We have already explained the reason for this.

His saying "alone" (wahidan) has two interpretations. The first: I created him alone, having no wealth and no children.

The second: I created him alone, with no one sharing with Me in his creation, and this is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira according to the view of most of the exegetes.﴾

And His saying: ﴿And I granted him extensive wealth﴾. Concerning it there are many opinions. The first: that it was a thousand dinars; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

And from Sufyan: four thousand dinars. Qatadah said: six thousand dinars.

And from Mujahid, in some narrations: one hundred thousand dinars.

The first opinion is well known, because accounting extends to it and then it ends.

And from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab: a monthly yield after a monthly yield.

It has also been reported that he had a garden in al-Ta'if whose income did not cease in winter or summer.

It is said: it is the wealth that encompasses all forms of gain, from trade, crops, livestock and other things.

And from Ibn ʿAbbas in some narrations: he had camels kept for breeding, horses grazing in pasture, and cattle, namely camels, cows and sheep, as well as gold, silver and other things.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 13:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And sons present with him﴾. In the tafsir it is said that he had [ten] sons. It is also said: thirteen.

It is also said: other than that.

And His words ﴿shuhudan﴾ mean: present, who do not leave his side because of need or out of fear.

(Narrated by Muslim.)

Of his sons, two embraced Islam: Khalid ibn al-Walid and Hisham ibn al-Walid. The rest died in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam).

And His saying: ﴿And I made smooth (ways) for him, smoothing (them) well.﴾ At-tamhid is preparation and making ready.

It is also said: I widened the matter for him, widening (it).

(It is said): I spread out for him what lies between Yemen and Syria.

That is, in trade.

It is also said: at-tamhid is the facilitating of the means of livelihood, as if everything he sought and desired from its means was made easy for him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 15–16:

And His saying: ﴿Then he hopes that I will increase him.﴾ It is related that when the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned what Allah the Exalted had prepared for the Muslims of the bliss of Paradise, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: "I am the most prosperous of you and the one with the most sons, so I am more deserving of Paradise than you." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Then he hopes that I will increase him. No!﴾ That is: I will not increase him.

It is also said that this refers to the worldly life, and that he became poor after that and was in need.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was obstinate toward Our signs.﴾ That is: opposing (mu'anidan).

It is also said: denying (jahidan).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 15–16:

And His saying: ﴿Then he hopes that I will increase him.﴾ It is related that when the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned what Allah the Exalted had prepared for the Muslims of the bliss of Paradise, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: "I am the most prosperous of you and the one with the most sons, so I am more deserving of Paradise than you." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Then he hopes that I will increase him. No!﴾ That is: I will not increase him.

It is also said that this refers to the worldly life, and that he became poor after that and was in need.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was obstinate toward Our signs.﴾ That is: opposing (mu'anidan).

It is also said: denying (jahidan).

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 17:**

And His saying: ﴿I will overwhelm him with a rugged ascent﴾. Al-irhaq (overwhelming, burdening) in the language means: to force a man to bear something (the thing).

And His saying: ﴿a rugged ascent﴾. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "It is a mountain of fire, he is made to climb it for seventy autumns, then he is thrown down from it, and so on forever in it."

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi (al-Tirmidhi) mentioned it in his book, and it is narrated that it is a rock of fire: when he places his hand upon it, it melts, and when he lifts it, it returns.

Al-Kalbi said: He is dragged from the front with chains, and struck from behind with maces. When he climbs up onto it, he is thrown down, like this, forever.

It is also said that al-su'ud (the ascent) is a steep incline.

And this statement is close to what we have mentioned.

The Qur'anic phrase here is ﴿Indeed he reflected﴾ (74:18, the statement about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira).

Al-Sam'ani's commentary, translated:

Allah's words, ﴿Indeed he reflected﴾, meaning: he pondered (tadabbur).

And His words, ﴿and he calculated﴾, which also means reflection (tafakkur).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 19:

And His saying: ﴿Then he was killed, how he calculated.﴾ That is: "He was cursed, how he calculated."

The author of al-Nazm said: its meaning is: "He was cursed in whatever state he calculated (what he calculated)."

Translation of the passage:

And His saying: ﴿Then, woe to him, how he calculated﴾ is for emphasis, and its meaning is what we have explained.

Note on the quotation: the Arabic gives "ثم قتل كيف قدر" which, in the standard text of 74:20, reads ﴿ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾, meaning "Then may he be killed, how he calculated." I should correct my rendering above: the verse is "Then, may he be killed, how he calculated," not "woe to him."

Corrected translation:

And His saying: ﴿Then may he be killed, how he calculated﴾ is for emphasis, and its meaning is what we have explained.

And his saying, ﴿Then he considered﴾: that is, by his opinion and intellect, regarding the matter of the Prophet.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated in his book, with his chain, from Mujahid that the polytheists gathered at the house of al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and said: "This season is coming, and people will arrive during it, and they will ask us about this man. If they ask us, we shall say: he is a poet."

Al-Walid said: "They hear his speech and know that he is not a poet."

They said: "We shall say: he is a madman." He said: "They see him and his speech, and they know that he is sensible."

They said: "We shall say he is a soothsayer (kahin)."

He said: "They have seen the soothsayers, and they will know that he is not a soothsayer."

They said: "Then what shall we say?" So then he reflected, and planned, and considered.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 22–24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then he frowned and scowled﴾, meaning: he contracted his face.

It is said of one who contracts his face: "his face is basir (scowling)."

It is also said: al-'ubus (frowning) is after the discussion, and al-busur (scowling) is before the discussion.

The more sound view is that both have one meaning, and He only said this because when a person is troubled by a matter and begins to reflect on it, his face becomes frowning, as one who is averse to something.

Then, when al-Walid had done all that he did for the people, [he] said: "Say: he is a sorcerer, for the sorcerer creates hatred between those who love one another, and creates love between those who hate one another, and Muhammad is like that." So they went out and gathered upon this statement, and they began to say to everyone they met: "He is a sorcerer." This is the meaning of His exalted saying: ﴿So he said, "This is nothing but sorcery imparted"﴾, meaning: the Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿imparted﴾ means: he transmits it from another.

They used to say: "He learns it from the slave boy of Ibn al-Hadrami," and it was said: from someone else.

His saying: ﴿Then he turned away and was arrogant﴾, meaning: he turned away and became proud.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 25:

His words: ﴿This is nothing but the word of a human being.﴾ That is, the Qur'an is the word of a human being, not the word of Allah, the Exalted.

Allah's words, ﴿Soon I shall cast him into Saqar﴾: "Soon I shall enter him" (sa-udkhiluhu). Saqar is one of the names of Jahannam (Hell).

Ibn 'Abbas said: It is the fifth level (daraka), and the levels are seven in total in the Qur'an: Jahannam, Laza, al-Jahim, Saqar, Sa'ir, al-Hawiyah, and al-Hutamah.
"And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what Saqar is?﴾ He said it to magnify the matter of Saqar."

And His saying: ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾. Mujahid said: It does not leave them alive so that they may rest, nor dead so that they may be relieved, and this is the meaning of God's saying: ﴿Neither dying therein nor living﴾.

It is also said: ﴿It leaves nothing and spares nothing﴾ means it leaves no flesh and no bone. (And spares nothing) means: when it has burned everything, it leaves nothing, because they return as a new creation.

It has also been said: it leaves no one of the disbelievers, meaning it takes all the disbelievers and does not spare them from the punishment for any period; that is, it burns them forever.

In some tafsir works: that everything grows weary and bored, except Hellfire.

And His saying: ﴿Scorching to the human being﴾, that is, burning.

Abu Razin said: It burns them until they become black like the dark night.

It was also said: "Scorching to the human being" means it scorches the flesh until the bone shows (talwah al-'azm).

It is also said that its meaning is that the skin of their bodies shows (talwah) in the fire; this was related from Mujahid.

It was also said: "Scorching to the human being," that is, thirst-inducing to the human being. The poet said:

(He gave me to drink on a ladle of water a drink... that Allah, the Rabb and the Ghawadi, gave him to drink.)

And His saying: ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾, meaning: of the guardians of Hell (al-zabaniyya) and the keepers of the Fire (khazanat al-nar).

In the tafsir (exegesis) it is related that the distance from the shoulder of one of them to the other shoulder is a year's journey, and he takes hold with his palm as much as the number of the tribes of Rabi'a and Mudar, and he pushes seventy thousand into the Fire with a single push.

It is also said: ninety thousand. Their eyes are like flashing lightning, and their teeth are like the horns of cows.

Al-Kalbi mentioned that they have helpers and soldiers whose number none knows except God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 31:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire but angels﴾. The occasion of the revelation of this verse was that when the Prophet informed them of the number of the Zabaniyah (the guardians of Hell), Abu Jahl said: "Muhammad appears to be threatening you with nineteen, while you are numerous! Will you not pair up with them, so that every ten of you may go against one of them and push him down?"

Abu al-Asad ibn Kaldah, who was a man of Banu Jumah, said: "I will go ahead of you to the Sirat (the bridge over Hell). I will push away ten with my right shoulder and nine with my left shoulder, and we will cross over into Paradise."

Kaldah ibn Usayd said: "I will suffice you against seventeen; you suffice me against two." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And We have not made the keepers of the Fire but angels﴾, meaning: these nineteen are from the angels, and how will you be able to withstand them? It is related that when the Muslims heard this from them, they said: "Do you measure the angels against the blacksmiths?" That is: (the jailers).

﴿And We have not made their number but a trial for those who disbelieve, so that those who were given the Book may be certain, and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Book and the believers may not doubt, and that those in whose hearts is a disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guide whom He wills. And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him.﴾

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We have not made their number but a trial for those who disbelieve﴾, that is: a bounty and a affliction, to the extent that they said what they said.

His words: ﴿So that those who were given the Book may be certain﴾, that is: so that those who were given the Book may be certain that Muhammad spoke what he spoke from Allah the Exalted, for it agreed with this number that was (mentioned) in the Torah and the Gospel.

His words: ﴿and those who believe may increase in faith﴾, that is: those among the People of the Book who believed will increase in faith.

It has also been said: all the believers will increase in faith when they see that what the Prophet said agrees with what the People of the Book have related.

His words: ﴿and those who were given the Book and the believers may not doubt﴾, that is: they will not be in doubt about the number when they find the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an in agreement on this number.

His words: ﴿and that those in whose hearts is a disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾, that is: how did Allah mention this number and specify the Zabaniyah with it? This is the explanation of His words: ﴿but a trial for those who disbelieve﴾.

His words: ﴿Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guide whom He wills﴾, meaning: just as He led the disbelievers astray by this number, and guided the believers to accept it, thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guide whom He wills, by what He sends down of the Qur'an.

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾. It is related that when the disbelievers heard this number, they said: "How small this number is!" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾, that is: He has hosts besides this number, whose number none knows but Him.

His words: ﴿And it is not but a reminder to mankind﴾, that is: this verse is an admonition and a lesson for mankind.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay, by the moon﴾. "Nay" (kallā) is a rejection of what they had said.

And His words: ﴿by the moon﴾ begin an oath.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 33:

And His saying: ﴿And the night when it turns back﴾. It is also read: ﴿when it turns back﴾ (idhā dabara), meaning: it turned away and departed.

And His saying: ﴿when it turns back﴾, meaning: when it comes after the day.

It is narrated that Abdullah ibn Abbas was asked about His saying: ﴿And the night when it turns back﴾, and he said to the questioner: "Wait." Then, when the muezzin called to the dawn prayer, he said: "This is the time when the night has turned back."

Some scholars have denied this reading, saying: "Idha dabara" is only said of the back of a camel.

The correct position is what we have explained, and both are well-known readings.

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: dabara and adbara have the same meaning.

And His saying: ﴿And the morning when it brightens﴾ — i.e., it became clear and shone.

It is said: "The woman unveiled (safarat) her face" (saffarat al-mar'ah 'an wajhiha), and "the man swept (safara) his house" when he cleaned it until he uncovered the dust of the house.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, it is one of the greatest (calamities)﴾ meaning: the Resurrection is one of the great matters.

It is also said: "the greatest" refers to the levels of Hell (darakat jahannam).

And His words: ﴿Indeed, it is one of the greatest﴾ meaning: Saqar is one of the levels of Hell (darakat jahannam), so it returns to what we have mentioned.

And His saying: ﴿a warner to mankind﴾, meaning: a warning to mankind.

Al-Nahhas mentioned that he returned to His saying:

﴿Arise﴾, meaning: arise as a warner to mankind.
Verse 37 of this surah reads: ﴿for whoever among you wills to go forward or to fall behind﴾. That is, he advances toward faith or falls behind from it.
Its meaning: "Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned" (Q. 74:38). That is, "rahina" means "murtahina," held as a pledge.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 39:

And His saying: ﴿Except the companions of the right hand﴾. They are not held in pledge, because they have no sins.

Zadhan narrated from ʿAli: they are the children of the Muslims.

It was also said: they are the prophets.

It was also said: they are those who are given their book in their right hands.

It was also said: they are those who were taken from the loins of Adam on the right side, and God Most High said to them: "These are for Paradise, and I do not care."

And from Ibn ʿAbbas: they are the angels.

In gardens. That is, orchards.

And His saying: ﴿They will ask one another about the guilty: "What has brought you into Saqar?"﴾ That is: what has caused you to enter Saqar? They asked about this because they did not know the sins [of those being asked]. This holds if we take it to refer to the angels and the children of the Muslims. But if we take it to refer to others, then it is a question asked with knowledge, and it is permissible for a person to ask about another while knowing his condition.

And His saying: ﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment until there came to us the certainty.﴾ That is: death.
And His saying: ﴿And we used to deny the Day of Judgment until there came to us the certainty.﴾ That is: death.

And His saying: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾, because they are disbelievers, so there will be no intercessor for them, and even if there were one, it would not benefit them.

In the exegesis: this is when a group of the believers come out of the Fire through the intercession of the prophets, the messengers, the angels, the scholars, and the truthful (al-siddiqin). All of this is related in the reports, and the disbelievers remain in the Fire specifically.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ Hmm, need to be careful: the translation should be plain inside the markers.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿So what is the matter with them, turning away from the reminder?﴾ That is: the admonition and the lesson.

And His saying: ﴿As if they were startled donkeys﴾. It is recited as ﴿mustanfarah﴾ with a fatha on the fa'.

And His saying: ﴿mustanfirah﴾ means fleeing, running away.

And His saying: ﴿mustanfarah﴾ means: terrified, frightened.

And His saying: ﴿They flee from a lion (qaswarah)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas and Abu Hurayra said: it is the lion.

Ibn ʿAbbas also said: In Arabic it is called al-asad (lion), in Abyssinian (Habashi) it is called al-qaswarah, in Persian shir, and in Nabataean aryā.

And from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, regarding ﴿from a lion﴾: they are the archers (al-naqqabun).

It was also said: they are the archers who shoot arrows (rumat al-nabl).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 52:

And His saying: ﴿Nay, but every man among them desires that he be given scrolls spread out﴾. It is related that the disbelievers said: "We will not believe in you, O Muhammad, until you bring each one of us a book from God stating, 'Believe in Muhammad, for he is My messenger.'"

Their saying: ﴿Nay⁠﴾ means: they will not be given these scrolls.

It is also said: ﴿Nay⁠﴾ means: even if they were given these scrolls, they would not believe.

Their saying: ﴿Nay, rather they do not fear the Hereafter⁠﴾ means: if they feared it, they would not have sought these things.
"And His saying: ﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder﴾ means: the Qur'an is an admonition and a lesson."

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it﴾, meaning: let him be admonished by it and take a lesson from it. Then He attributed the will back to Himself, and so He said:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 74, verse 56:

﴿And they do not remember except that Allah wills.﴾ That is: they do not take heed or admonish themselves except by My will.

And His saying: ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness.﴾ That is: He is worthy that He should keep eternal in Paradise whoever fears Him, and does not set up any god along with Him.

﴿And worthy of forgiveness﴾ That is: whoever fears Me and does not set up any god along with Me, I am worthy to forgive him.

In this there is a sound (musnad) report through the narration of Anas from the Prophet (ﷺ) to this effect, which Abu 'Isa (al-Tirmidhi) mentioned in his book.

And from Muhammad ibn al-Nadr ibn al-Harith regarding this verse: His saying ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾ means: I am worthy that I be feared by the abandonment of sins, ﴿and worthy of forgiveness﴾ That is: and I am worthy to forgive the sinners if they do not fear Me.

Al-Azhari mentioned, regarding His saying ﴿Nay, every one of them desires that he be given open scrolls﴾, another view: it is that the polytheists said: "The children of Israel, when one of them committed a sin, his sin would appear written on the door of his house, so why is it not the case for us if we are sinners?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and informed, in this sense, that He does not do that for this community, and that this was specific to the children of Israel.

And Allah knows best.
